finding_assessments.assessment: No fatal typing defect or missing established theorem: the radicand is nonnegative by elementary ordered-field algebra already available in the complete-real-field context.
finding_assessments.argument: For t=0, distributivity gives t²=0. For t≠0, trichotomy and closure (or existing square-positive lemma) give t²>0. Each of a²,b² is therefore zero or positive; if one is zero their sum is the other, otherwise positive-cone addition applies. Hence a²+b²>=0 and the square-root theorem applies on its exact domain.
finding_assessments.proposal: Optional Remarks domain derivation only; the original entire Definition is byte-identical. No new supplier or dependency edge.

finding_assessments.argument: Low case δ=(a-s²)/(2s+1)>0, h=δ/(1+δ) satisfies0<h<1 and h<δ by positive scaling. High case δ=(s²-a)/(2s)>0, h=sδ/(s+δ) satisfies0<h<s and h<δ. All denominators are positive under the current case hypotheses. No density/completeness or choice axiom is needed for these witnesses.

finding_assessments.assessment: The flagged weak nonnegative sum/product and zero-square inferences are elementary consequences of the complete ordered-field premise F3 and nonzero-square supplier F5. No invalid modulus law or missing helper was found.
finding_assessments.argument: A square is zero in the zero case and positive otherwise. A sum/product of nonnegative elements is zero or the unchanged positive element when a relevant input iszero; otherwise positive-cone closure applies. A sum of two such squares can vanish only if both coordinates vanish. These give exactly the signs needed for unique roots and monotonic squaring.
finding_assessments.proposal: Expand zero/positive cases in the existing Proof steps1.3,2.1,3.1,3.2,5.1 without changing numbering, hypotheses, Statement, dependencies or conclusions.

finding_assessments.assessment: The derived weak-case sum property attributed to the ordered field is valid; a direct zero/positive case split explains the attribution. No false claim or missing prerequisite.
finding_assessments.argument: If two nonnegative elements include a positive one, either the other iszero and the sum is unchanged, or both arepositive and positive-cone addition applies. This proves the precise b+a>0 fact used in2.1/2.2. Def-ordered-field includes ordinary field addition/zero laws through its field datum.
